note: Fee-on-transfer token: a taxed transfer emits TWO Transfer events with the SAME sender -- 99% of the amount to the intended recipient and 1% credited to the token contract itself, which accumulates the fee for later swap-back. Both legs are in the receipt, so the split is reproducible from eth_getLogs alone with no tracing. The fee is a floored integer division, so the realised rate equals 100 bps up to a rounding residue of at most one base unit; the exact rational for the cited transaction is in evidence.taxBpsExactRational. Confirmed on 11 independent two-leg transfers, 11 of them with the pool 0x988a44a15a71dfad11b4e17a11ede7cb5e373b79 as an endpoint, so pool-side transfers ARE taxed -- which is what makes the token unsafe as a routing hop rather than merely unusual. Failure modes by position in a router path: (1) as INPUT or INTERMEDIATE -- the destination pool receives only 99% of amountSent, so pool.swap(amount0Out, ...) reverts K() because the demanded output assumed the full amountSent; (2) as TERMINAL OUTPUT -- no next pool and no K() revert, but the user receives 99% of the quoted amountOut, silently violating the minAmountOut slippage promise (delivered < quoted). Both modes are unsafe.
